Since useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to this hook and no longer receives the rule group, federated Mimir rule groups will incorrectly be reported as editable/deletable, allowing users to attempt unsupported mutations on federated rules.

Rule view link lost the returnTo parameter

The deleted GrafanaRuleLoader built the list-item href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` so navigating to a rule from the list and back preserved the list context. The new GrafanaRuleListItem creates the URL without returnTo, so users clicking a rule from the filtered list lose their filter/list context when returning. Confirm this drop is intentional; if not, restore the returnTo parameter.

getGrafanaRuleKey emits a stray '}' in the generated key

The template literal ends with `${rule.uid}}`, adding a literal closing brace to every grafana rule key. Harmless for uniqueness today but it is a typo that will confuse anyone extending the key format, and since this key mechanism was just re-wired (and is the key that should be passed to GrafanaRuleListItem per the missing-key finding), fix the stray character.

showDivider expression wraps single values in arrays and is misleading

`[canPause, canSilence, shouldShowDeclareIncidentButton, canDuplicate].some(Boolean) && [canExport].some(Boolean)` — the second clause is equivalent to plain `canExport`. Beyond style, this makes the divider logic hard to verify and suggests an intended condition that was never written (e.g. shareUrl should probably also gate the divider, otherwise 'Copy link' can appear directly above/below a divider inconsistently when canExport is false). Simplify to an explicit expression.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The applyTemplateVariables method is called with request.filters as the third parameter, but this parameter is not used in the corresponding test setup.

false_positives.candidate:
$__auto and other interval macros are frozen to the full-range value across all split chunks

By interpolating with datasource.applyTemplateVariables before splitting, built-in macros like $__auto (and any interval-derived variable) are resolved once against the original request's range/interval and then reused verbatim in every sub-request's narrower time range. Previously the backend resolved these per sub-request, allowing each chunk to use a range-appropriate value. The new test in querySplitting.test.ts ('Interpolates queries before execution') hard-codes the expectation that $__auto becomes 5m for all three daily chunks, which codifies the behavior change; for range-sensitive macros this can change results (e.g., count_over_time windows no longer adapting per chunk). This should be confirmed as intended and, if so, documented, since it silently changes query semantics for existing dashboards.

Double template interpolation in the shard-splitting path

runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables(), but the resulting queries are then passed to runSplitQuery(), which (after this PR) calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on the same targets (querySplitting.ts:299). Template interpolation is not idempotent in general: if a variable's value itself contains text that looks like a variable reference or a `$` character (common in label-filter values, regex patterns, or chained variables), the second pass will re-interpolate the already-substituted value and corrupt the expression or step. Either runShardSplitQuery should skip interpolation and let runSplitQuery do it once, or runSplitQuery needs a way to know the targets are already interpolated. There is also no test covering this double-interpolation scenario.

Interpolating before the $__range guard defeats the no-split check for range-variable queries

runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on each target before the partition step. The subsequent querySupportsSplitting() check relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) detecting a literal $__range/$__range_s variables in the expression (see the comment at querySplitting.ts:285-287: queries with $__range must not be split because the backend interpolates $__range against the split sub-range). After applyTemplateVariables runs, $__range has already been replaced with the full original time range, so isQueryWithRangeVariable never matches and such queries are now split into per-day chunks with the full-range value baked into the expr. Every sub-request then aggregates over the whole range instead of its chunk, producing duplicated/incorrect data for any query using $__range. The interpolation must happen after the range-variable check, or the check must run on the pre-interpolation expression.

true_positives.golden_comment: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
traceID no longer guaranteed in data-egress log event

The old code explicitly appended `traceID` from `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` to the "Plugin Request Completed" log parameters. The new code drops that and relies on the contextual logger (`FromContext`) to surface a trace ID. Unless `log.WithContextualAttributes`/`ConcreteLogger.FromContext` is guaranteed to attach the trace ID from the context, this removes the traceID field from the grafana-data-egress event, breaking correlation between plugin egress logs and traces. This should be verified or the traceID explicitly re-added.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

false_positives.candidate:
LoggerMiddleware silently loses pluginId/endpoint/traceID unless ContextualLoggerMiddleware is composed first

The "Plugin Request Completed" log line (the grafana-data-egress audit event) previously included pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID explicitly. It now relies entirely on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up contextual attributes that were injected by the separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware. Nothing enforces that composition: if LoggerMiddleware is used without ContextualLoggerMiddleware earlier in the chain (e.g. in tests, alternative wire setups, or future reordering of CreateMiddlewares), the audit logs will silently contain no pluginId, endpoint, user or datasource identifiers and no traceID. There is no test covering the LoggerMiddleware output fields after this change to catch such a regression.

No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware

A new middleware with non-trivial behavior (attribute selection, nil checks on DataSourceInstanceSettings and User) is added without any test coverage. There is also no test verifying that the LoggerMiddleware's output actually contains the previously-present fields (pluginId, endpoint, traceID, uname, dsName) after the refactor, which is the main behavioral risk of this PR.

Stream endpoints are not enriched with the contextual logger

SubscribeStream, PublishStream and RunStream are passed through without calling instrumentContext, so any downstream logging for streaming requests will lack pluginId/endpoint/dsName/uname. RunStream is a long-lived request where such context is especially valuable. This matches the old behavior for the logger, but since the PR introduces a dedicated middleware whose sole purpose is contextual logging, the omission is now more conspicuous.

Test still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after rename to MetricsMiddleware

The middleware was renamed from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware, but the test function is still called TestInstrumentationMiddleware, which is confusing for anyone searching for tests of the renamed component.

true_positives.golden_comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Count-then-insert race allows the device limit to be exceeded

CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices in one session and, if the count is below deviceLimit, performs the insert in a separate session/transaction. Two (or many) concurrent requests from different new devices can each observe count < limit and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. The check-and-insert must be atomic (e.g. a single conditional insert/transaction with a lock, or a unique count constraint) to actually enforce the limit under load, which is exactly the scenario (burst of anonymous requests) this feature targets.

true_positives.golden_comment: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
ErrDeviceLimitReached returned raw from Authenticate produces an opaque 500-style auth failure

When TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, Authenticate returns that error directly. The authn layer will treat this as an internal authentication error rather than an expected 'too many devices' condition, so users over the limit will get a generic error (likely 500 Internal Server Error on every request) with no indication of the cause. There is no mapping of this sentinel error to an appropriate HTTP status (e.g. 403/429) or user-facing message anywhere in this PR, making the feature effectively brick anonymous access without explanation once the limit is hit (combined with the cache bug, intermittently).

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Expiry window logic: a device that exists but is older than 30 days can never be updated when limit is reached, and error semantics conflate cases

updateDevice's WHERE clause requires updated_at BETWEEN (UpdatedAt-30d) and (UpdatedAt+1m). If the count of active devices has reached the limit but the requesting device's row exists yet falls outside that window (e.g. clock skew or a device idle just past 30 days before cleanup runs), the UPDATE affects 0 rows and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached even though this device is one of the 'expired' rows that shouldn't count toward the limit. The store then neither updates nor deletes the stale row, so the device stays locked out until the 61-day cleanup job removes it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Device limit is bypassed after the first rejected request due to localCache set before the DB call

In tagDeviceUI, localCache.SetDefault(key, ...) is executed before calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. If CreateOrUpdateDevice fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the device ID is still marked as tagged in the 29-minute local cache. On the user's next request, the cache hit makes tagDeviceUI return nil without touching the database, so Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds. The net effect is that the device limit only rejects each new device once per ~29 minutes; every subsequent request from that device authenticates successfully. The cache entry must only be set after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice (and any error path should invalidate it).

false_negatives.golden_comment: Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

false_positives.candidate:
AnonymousDeviceLimit exposed to all frontend clients including anonymous users

AnonymousDeviceLimit is included in the frontend settings DTO served to every requester, including unauthenticated/anonymous visitors. This leaks an instance's configured capacity limit (useful reconnaissance for abuse: an attacker knows exactly how many spoofed X-Grafana-Device-Id values are needed to lock out legitimate anonymous users, since the limit is enforced per arbitrary client-supplied device IDs). Consider only exposing it to signed-in admins, or not exposing it at all if no frontend code consumes it — no frontend usage is added in this PR, only the type declarations.

New device_limit setting is undocumented and lacks validation

The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting is parsed with MustInt64(0) but has no documentation (configure docs/conf defaults), and negative values are not rejected. A negative value behaves like 0 (limit disabled) due to the `deviceLimit > 0` check, silently ignoring the user's intent; a validation error for negative values would be clearer. Also note that device_limit interacts with the 61-day retention (keepFor) in impl.go while the limit counts only devices active in the last 30 days — this asymmetry is nowhere documented for operators.

TagDevice moved onto the synchronous request path, removing the previous timeout/async isolation

The old code ran TagDevice in a goroutine with a 2-minute context.WithTimeout, so database slowness in the anon_device table never delayed or failed anonymous authentication. The new code calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously inside Authenticate using the request context. Now every anonymous request performs up to two extra DB round trips (COUNT + INSERT/UPDATE) before the identity is returned; a slow or locked anon_device table will hang or fail all anonymous access. If the synchronous behavior is required to surface the limit error, consider at minimum retaining a timeout so DB issues cannot degrade anonymous auth.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Successful cleanup batches are logged at Error level

In CleanAnnotations, CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags the new code calls r.log.Error(...) for every batch, including fully successful ones (e.g. `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...)` and the matching "cleaned annotations" / "Tags to clean" / "cleaned tags" calls at lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579). This is debug/diagnostic output, and now every annotation cleanup job run on every Grafana instance will emit Error-level log lines with the full list of deleted annotation IDs, polluting logs, potentially triggering alerting on error logs, and leaking annotation IDs. These should be Debug level (and drop the always-nil "err" field and the huge "ids" slice).

true_positives.golden_comment: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute without mention in PR description

The cleanup loop ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, but the PR description only discusses the annotation deadlock fix. This makes all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs, query history) run 10x more often, which increases recurring database load for all users and is a behavior change that should be documented in the PR description / changelog. Note also that the per-run timeout in clean() remains 9 minutes, so the intended cadence is unclear; if a cleanup cycle takes several minutes, jobs effectively run back-to-back.

true_positives.golden_comment: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete logs with the bare logger, dropping name/kind context

In Delete, `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` is used instead of the `log` variable built two lines above (which includes name, kind and method). Any error logged in Delete will lack the identifying fields, unlike every other method in this file. Likely a copy-paste oversight.

true_positives.golden_comment: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
DeleteCollection records legacy result with the storage metrics recorder

In DeleteCollection's goroutine, the outcome of `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` is recorded via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection latencies and failures are therefore attributed to unified storage, corrupting the dual-writer metrics used to monitor migration progress.

true_positives.golden_comment: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Delete records 'name' where the resource 'kind' label is expected

On success, Delete calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passing the object name as the label where every other call passes `options.Kind`. This produces unbounded/high-cardinality metric label values (one per object name) and inconsistent series compared to the failure path on line 103 which uses options.Kind.

false_positives.candidate:
Async legacy writes are canceled when the request context ends

In Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection, the goroutine that writes to legacy storage derives its 10s-timeout context from the incoming request context (`ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). As soon as the API request returns, the request context is canceled, so the deferred legacy write/delete is aborted with 'context canceled' rather than running for its timeout. This defeats the stated purpose of the mode ('write to legacy as a safe measure') and silently leaves the two stores divergent. The goroutines should use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (or background) as the parent.

Legacy Delete failures on NotFound are treated as errors

The old Delete tolerated apierrors.IsNotFound from the legacy store (expected when an object exists only in unified storage, which is the common case in mode 3 after migration backfill gaps). The new code records any legacy Delete error, including NotFound, as a failure metric. In mode 3, objects created before backfill will routinely 404 in legacy, producing persistent false failure signals.

Legacy Update reuses the request's objInfo, so legacy can write different data than storage

The previous implementation wrapped objInfo so the legacy store received exactly the object that unified storage wrote (via updateWrapper). The new code passes the original objInfo to d.Legacy.Update in a goroutine, so the legacy store re-computes the updated object from its own (possibly stale) current state. If legacy and unified have diverged (e.g., an earlier async legacy write was canceled or failed), the legacy copy can end up with different content than the authoritative unified copy. The updateWrapper mechanism was removed without a replacement guarantee.

Legacy write failures are swallowed with no logging or reconciliation

Previously, errors from the legacy store were at least logged. In the new goroutines, the error from d.Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection is only converted into a boolean for a metric; it is never logged and no reconciliation/retry is queued. Since mode 3 is the last dual-write stage before cutting over to unified storage, silent legacy failures mean data loss in the legacy store with no operator-visible signal beyond an aggregate counter and no way to recover the missed write.

Storage failures in Create and Update are recorded as legacy metrics

When d.Storage.Create fails (line 45) or d.Storage.Update fails (line 129), the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` even though the legacy store was never contacted. These failures and their durations are attributed to legacy storage, skewing the dual-writer observability data. Both should be recordStorageDuration.

TestMode3_Get creates its own registry instead of the shared one

TestMode3_Get declares a local `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` while every other mode-3 test uses the package-level `p`. This is inconsistent and, if the dual writer registers metrics in NewDualWriter, would panic on double registration in other tests or mask registration issues; the unrelated change to TestMode1_Get that moved `p` to package scope suggests this local declaration is an oversight.

Unit tests never verify that the async legacy write actually happens

Mode 3's defining behavior is 'write to unified, then asynchronously write to legacy', but none of the tests assert that Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection are invoked (e.g., via m.AssertExpectations or waiting on the goroutine with mock.AssertEventually). The tests return immediately after the unified call, so the goroutines may not have run; a regression that drops the legacy write entirely (or is canceled immediately, as in the context bug) would still pass. Also the error-path test cases set up legacy mock expectations that are never exercised or verified.

true_positives.golden_comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
No cache recheck after acquiring the write lock (missing double-checked locking)

After the RLock fast path fails, GetWebAssets acquires the exclusive lock and unconditionally re-reads the manifest from disk/CDN and overwrites entryPointAssetsCache. If N concurrent requests arrive before the cache is populated (e.g. at startup in non-Dev mode), every one of them performs the file read serially instead of one goroutine populating the cache and the rest reusing it. The fix is incomplete double-checked locking: after taking the write lock, the function should re-read entryPointAssetsCache and return it if non-nil (for the non-Dev case).

false_negatives.golden_comment: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

false_positives.candidate:
Exclusive lock held across file I/O and CDN HTTP request

GetWebAssets holds entryPointAssetsCacheMu (write lock) for the entire duration of readWebAssetsFromFile and, if a CDN URL is ever set, the blocking HTTP request in readWebAssetsFromCDN (currently the cdn variable is hardcoded to "", but that is an existing call path). In Dev mode this happens on every call. A slow or hanging CDN request would block every other caller of GetWebAssets, including the RLock fast-path readers, stalling request handling. Consider loading the result outside the lock and only taking the lock briefly to publish it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
true_positives.matched_candidate:
enableSqlExpressions is dead logic and always returns false

The function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns `false` in both branches, making the feature-toggle check meaningless dead code. Since the intent of the PR is to disable SQL expressions entirely, this is misleading: readers and linters will assume the flag still has an effect. Either remove the function and the toggle check entirely (and return an unconditional error), or actually honor the flag if that was intended. As written it also guarantees the QueryTypeSQL path can never be enabled, which should be stated clearly in the code rather than hidden behind dead branches.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

false_positives.candidate:
Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is wrong/misleading

When a user submits a SQL expression, they get `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"`. The feature is implemented but disabled for security reasons (CVE-2024-9264). The message should say something like "SQL expressions are disabled" so users understand this is a deliberate state and can find the associated documentation/flag. The current wording will generate confusion and unnecessary support issues.

Execute overwrites NoData result with empty TableData

In `SQLCommand.Execute`, when `frame.Rows() == 0` the code sets `rsp.Values` to a `NoData` value, but then unconditionally overwrites `rsp.Values` with `TableData{Frame: frame}` on the next statement (lines 116-118). The NoData branch is dead code and downstream consumers will see an empty table instead of a NoData result. This is pre-existing, but since this PR touches Execute and leaves it in place, it is worth fixing while here.

Feature-disable check not applied to UnmarshalSQLCommand / legacy path

The new disable check was only added to `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` (pkg/expr/reader.go, QueryTypeSQL case). However `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (pkg/expr/sql_command.go) also constructs `SQLCommand` from user-supplied query JSON (`rn.Query["expression"]`) and does not perform any feature-toggle or disable check. If any code path (e.g. older frontend payloads handled through the raw-node unmarshal route in transform.go/parse.go) still dispatches to `UnmarshalSQLCommand` for `type: "sql"`, a user can still create SQL commands; while the stub DB now fails at Execute time, the parsing/validation code is still reachable and the intended hard disable is inconsistent. The disable should be enforced at command-construction level (or both entry points), not only one reader.

No tests updated for disabled SQL expressions; existing tests will fail or are now meaningless

The PR replaces the DuckDB-backed implementation with stubs that always return "not implemented", and removes the go-duck dependency, but includes no test changes. Any existing tests in pkg/expr/sql (TablesList) or SQL-command integration/e2e tests will now fail because RunCommands/QueryFramesInto always error. Additionally there are no new tests asserting that a QueryTypeSQL expression is rejected with the expected error from ReadQuery, nor that the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is blocked. A security-disable change should come with regression tests proving the CVE vector is closed.

SQL injection-prone string interpolation left in TablesList

`TablesList` still builds a DuckDB command via `fmt.Sprintf("SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')", rawSQL)` after only escaping single quotes. Although the stub DB now makes this unreachable-at-runtime, the unsafe interpolation pattern remains in the codebase and will be silently revived when a real implementation replaces the stub. The method should either be removed along with the DuckDB dependency, or rewritten to use parameterized command execution. Also note `ast[0]` in tablesFromAST panics on an empty AST slice.

true_positives.golden_comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds and lost index writes

BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for its whole duration, which (despite the perf cost) guaranteed only one index per NamespacedResource was ever built and published to the cache. Now the lock is only taken around `b.cache[key] = idx`. Two callers can build the same key concurrently: during `searchSupport.init` (multi-worker errgroup) and via `getOrCreateIndex` triggered by a watch event or a Search request arriving while init is still building. Consequences: (1) two bleveIndex objects exist for the same key; the loser of the last cache write keeps getting writes (e.g. from handleEvent) into an index that is no longer in the cache, so those documents silently vanish from search results — data loss for the index; (2) for file-backed indexes (`size > FileThreshold`), both builds call `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same directory, which will fail (index already exists) or corrupt the on-disk index. getOrCreateIndex's own TODO comment ("we don't want to block while anything is building, just the same key") confirms per-key serialization is required; this change removed even the coarse serialization without adding a per-key one.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

false_positives.candidate:
Data race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` in init's worker goroutines

In searchSupport.init, the loop over stats spawns goroutines (limited by initWorkers, so several run concurrently) that both execute `totalBatchesIndexed++` and assign `_, _, err = s.build(...)` where `err` is the outer function-scope variable declared at `stats, err := s.storage.GetResourceStats(...)`. These are unsynchronized concurrent read/writes of shared variables — a data race under Go's memory model (and `go test -race` will flag it), and the shared `err` can be clobbered by a later goroutine, causing a real build error to be lost so init reports success with a missing index. Each goroutine should use its own local counter/err (e.g. `i, e := 0, error(nil)` captured per closure), with totals aggregated after group.Wait().

Failed Init in constructor leaks the server's background context and goroutines

When s.Init(ctx) fails inside NewResourceServer, the function returns nil, err, but s.cancel() is never called. Init may have already started background work before failing — notably searchSupport.init's watch-event goroutine (started after WatchWriteEvents succeeds) and the lifecycle hooks' partial initialization. With no reference to the server retained by the caller, those goroutines and the cancelable context are leaked for the life of the process. The error path should call s.cancel() (or s.Stop) before returning.

Init ordering change: watch events consumed by searchSupport.init but broadcaster started after — event gap risk and misordering rationale

The diff moves initWatcher() to after s.search.init(). searchSupport.init internally starts its own WatchWriteEvents subscription, so this ordering is intentional (watch events are captured while the index builds). However, the server's broadcaster (used by the Watch RPC) is only started after the potentially long index build completes. During that window, Watch RPCs that do reach the server (the gRPC server may already be serving since the module server registers services before/around construction) will fail or block on s.broadcaster — notably s.broadcaster is nil until initWatcher succeeds, so a Watch call during init will nil-pointer panic on `s.broadcaster.Subscribe`. At minimum the nil broadcaster needs a guard, or initWatcher should run before search init (with search's own event subscription providing continuity, which is the pre-existing design).

NewResourceServer now performs full index build synchronously, changing the constructor contract for all callers

Init() (which builds the entire search index over all namespaces and can take a long time on large installations) is now invoked inside NewResourceServer, and any init failure makes the constructor return an error. Previously, callers such as embedded/in-process usage of the resource server (e.g. apiserver storage wiring, tests, single-binary Grafana where the unified storage may be created alongside other services) got a server immediately and initialization happened lazily or in the background. Those callers now block startup for the whole index build and will fail hard if the index build errors (e.g. transient DB issue during startup), where previously reads/writes could still be served. The PR description itself flags this ("Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily?") — the callers of NewResourceServer outside the storage-server target need to be audited; no such audit or feature flag is included.

Storage-server integration test disabled for postgres with no follow-up issue

The only integration test covering the storage-server target (which is exactly the code path changed by this PR — eager init of unified storage at startup) is now skipped for postgres with a TODO comment ("not working with postgres in Drone"). This means the main behavioral change in this PR (synchronous index init at startup) has no integration coverage on one of the two supported databases, and the failure cause is neither diagnosed nor tracked. Since this test is the regression guard for the change, the skip should be replaced by a fix or linked to a tracked issue.

Watch event goroutine has no termination path and panics on closed channel

The goroutine started at the end of init reads `v := <-events` in an infinite loop with no select on a done channel. When the storage backend closes the events channel (e.g. the SQL poller exits when b.done fires on Stop, which closes the stream), the receive yields nil forever and s.handleEvent(watchctx, nil) dereferences evt.Type/evt.Key, panicking the process. Additionally, because this uses context.Background(), there is no way to stop it on shutdown. Now that init runs in the constructor for the storage-server target, every server start creates this goroutine, so it must be tied to the server's cancelable context.

true_positives.golden_comment: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cleanup registers removal of literal "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias

In testCacheIDPForLogin, getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) uses the literal string "alias" rather than the constructed alias variable ("idp-alias-" + i). The registered cleanup will target a non-existent identity provider and either throw 404 during cleanup or silently fail, leaking the 20 created IDPs between test runs and potentially making subsequent runs fail on alias conflicts. The same bug exists at line 425 for "idp-alias-20".

false_negatives.golden_comment: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

false_positives.candidate:
Cached getForLogin loses the delegate's result ordering

When served from cache, getForLogin collects the IDPs into a HashSet and returns identityProviders.stream(), whereas the uncached/delegate path returns the delegate's stream, which for the JPA storage is ordered by alias. Callers that sort (like IdentityProviderBean) are unaffected, but any other consumer of IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin that relies on the ordering of the delegate (a behavioral difference between cached and uncached invocations) will see non-deterministic ordering only when the cache is warm. Use a LinkedHashSet or sort before returning to keep behavior consistent.

getLoginPredicate NPEs when an IDP has a null config map

The new clause in getLoginPredicate calls idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) whenever idp.getOrganizationId() != null. IdentityProviderModel.getConfig() can be null (e.g. models built programmatically or deserialized without a config map; other code in the codebase null-guards getConfig()). Any create/update/remove of an IDP that is linked to an organization but has a null config will now throw a NullPointerException inside registerIDPLoginInvalidation / registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate, breaking the write operation. Guard with idp.getConfig() == null || ... instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default KeyStore provider (e.g. SUN), not a BouncyCastle provider

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which on a stock JVM is the SUN provider, not BouncyCastle. Callers of this method (e.g. code in keycloak-common that fetches the provider to register it or relies on it being BC/BCFIPS, or that checks `getBouncyCastleProvider().getName()`) will silently get a provider that does not implement the BC algorithms they expect, leading to hard-to-diagnose NoSuchAlgorithmException failures. At minimum this is misleading for the interface contract documented as 'BouncyCastle security provider'; if BC is not available, throwing UnsupportedOperationException (as done for the other methods) would fail fast and predictably.

true_positives.golden_comment: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and written to, then discarded

In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, lines 114–115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write the r and s BigIntegers into them, and throw the results away; the actual encoding happens in the following statement. This is leftover debug/dead code that wastes work and confuses readers; it should be removed.

true_positives.golden_comment: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Indefinite-length DER (0x80) is returned as -1 and causes NegativeArraySizeException instead of a clean error

readLength() maps the indefinite-length marker 0x80 to -1. In readSequence(), a length of -1 makes the `while (length > 0)` loop simply skip parsing and return an empty list (silently accepting malformed input), and in readNext() the -1 propagates to read(-1), where `new byte[-1]` throws an uncaught NegativeArraySizeException rather than an IOException. Since BER indefinite-length encodings are not valid DER for ECDSA signatures, they should be rejected with an explicit IOException.

true_positives.golden_comment: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Adding abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider SPI implementations

The new `int order()` method was added to the public `CryptoProvider` interface as an abstract (non-default) method. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this SPI (custom crypto providers, adapters, older keycloak-client jars on the same classpath) will no longer compile and, if precompiled, will fail at runtime with an AbstractMethodError when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` on them. Since this is a public extension interface, the new method should have a default implementation (e.g., `default int order() { return 0; }`) to preserve binary compatibility.

false_positives.candidate:
Equal order() values across DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider make provider selection nondeterministic

DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order() == 200. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider previously threw an IllegalStateException when multiple providers were found; now it silently picks the first after sorting, but the sort is stable only relative to ServiceLoader iteration order, which depends on classpath ordering. In a deployment that (accidentally or intentionally) has more than one of these providers on the classpath, e.g. a FIPS environment where keycloak-crypto-fips1402 and keycloak-crypto-default are both present, the non-FIPS provider may win arbitrarily, silently disabling FIPS mode. Either the FIPS provider should have a strictly higher order, or ties among full-featured providers should still be reported as an error.

Most CryptoProvider operations throw UnsupportedOperationException, breaking authz-client features beyond ECDSA signature conversion

The provider registered via META-INF/services in the authz-client jar throws UnsupportedOperationException for getPemUtils(), getCertificateUtils(), getX509CertFactory(), getKeyFactory(), getSignature(), getAlgorithmProvider() etc. CryptoIntegration.init is now called from AuthzClient.create, so if this is the only provider discoverable via the AuthzClient classloader, any code path in keycloak-common/authz-client that touches those APIs will fail at runtime — for example parsing PEM keys/certificates for client JWT assertion signing, or JWKS handling. Previously, these paths worked whenever BC was on the classpath via DefaultCryptoProvider; now a working deployment can regress to UnsupportedOperationException. Each unsupported method should either be implemented with JCE defaults (as WildFlyElytronProvider does) or the design should ensure DefaultCryptoProvider is used when available.

Test uses one default-curve key pair for all algorithms and only checks round-trip, not interop with the BC implementation

The test generates a single key pair with KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC") without specifying a curve, so ES384/ES512 cases run with (typically) a P-256 key and only exercise zero-padding logic, never real 48/66-byte coordinates. More importantly, it only verifies that this provider's conversion round-trips with itself; it does not compare output against DefaultCryptoProvider/BouncyCastle (e.g., BCECDSACryptoProvider) to guarantee signature compatibility with what the Keycloak server produces/expects. A cross-check against the BC implementation per curve would catch subtle encoding mismatches (leading-zero handling, negative integers) that a self-round-trip cannot.

true_positives.golden_comment: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
getClientsWithPermission leaks the "Clients" all-resource name and ignores all-clients grants

getClientsWithPermission iterates resources found by type Clients and adds resource.getName() for each granted resource. The "Clients" all-resource itself has type Clients, so if the admin holds a scope permission on it (granted for all clients), the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set — a value that is not a client ID. Worse, the intended semantics of an all-clients grant (the caller should see every client) are not handled at all: callers filtering client lists by this set will get an empty/incorrect result even though the admin is allowed to act on all clients. The method should either translate an all-clients grant into the full client set or exclude the type-level resource from the iteration.

true_positives.golden_comment: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
NPE when the all-clients resource does not exist in hasPermission(ClientModel, String)

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when no per-client resource exists, the code calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately passes the result to authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource explicitly returns null when the resource type is unknown or no resource with that name exists (which is exactly the situation for realms initialized before this change, or if the "Clients" resource was never created). findByResource(server, null) will then throw a NullPointerException (or store-dependent error), turning a permission check into a 500 instead of returning false. The null case must be handled before calling findByResource.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

false_positives.candidate:
Client deletion throws UnsupportedOperationException with V2 enabled via the ClientRemovedEvent listener

AdminPermissions.registerListener() handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). Before this PR, MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override clients(), so the V1 ClientPermissions implementation was used and this call worked. Now clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). The listener guard only checks Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), which is typically enabled together with V2, so deleting any client in a realm where the fine-grained admin authz features are active will throw an exception inside the provider-event listener, likely failing or corrupting the client-removal flow. setPermissionsEnabled (and the other inherited V1 methods that no longer have a working implementation) need a no-op/compat implementation, or the listener must skip the clients branch for V2.

No migration for realms that already initialized the admin permissions client: new Clients resource and scopes are never created

AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null. Any realm that enabled admin permissions before this change has a resource server containing only the Users resource type and only the Users scopes (manage, view, impersonate, map-roles, manage-group-membership). The new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite) and the "Clients" all-resource will never be created for such realms. Consequences: creating a Clients scope permission will fail (getScope lookup fails or resource lookup in getOrCreateResource finds nothing and throws "Could not map resource object..."), and ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission can hit a null "Clients" resource (see separate NPE finding). A migration step (or extending init() to create missing scopes/resources for existing admin permission clients) is required.

canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token-exchange permission evaluation paths

canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException. This method is part of the ClientPermissions contract used by token-exchange admin/permission evaluation code that is not gated on the V2 feature flag; if any of those paths execute while V2 is enabled, the caller receives a 500 error instead of an authorization decision. Either the V2 implementation must provide a decision (e.g., delegate to the scope-based evaluation or deny), or all call sites must be verified to be unreachable under V2 — with the unreachable ones documented/tested. The same concern applies to the other thrown methods if any remaining code path (e.g., the registerListener cleanup path) invokes them.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance

false_positives.candidate:
Default-strategy (null) test runs without the rolling-updates feature enabled

In createInitialDeployment the ROLLING_UPDATES feature is only enabled when updateStrategy is non-null. The docs (advanced-configuration.adoc) state that while the rolling-updates feature is in preview it must be enabled or the operator will fail whenever the update spec is used. The null-strategy parameterization therefore exercises the CR update path without the feature, which per the documented contract is unsupported. If the operator is later changed to reject update-spec usage without the feature, this test will break; conversely, if the feature is not actually required for the default strategy, the documentation caution is misleading. Clarify the contract and align test and docs.

Feature-disabled case does not assert the new exit code 4

testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message 'Unable to use this command. The preview feature rolling-updates is not enabled.' but does not verify the process exit code is CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4). The exit code is the documented, scriptable contract for this tool (the guide documents exit code 4 specifically for the disabled-feature case), so a regression that prints the message but returns the wrong exit code would go unnoticed. Add assertEquals(4, cliResult.exitCode()) or equivalent.

true_positives.golden_comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Global canManage() grants manage access with only the VIEW scope

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (no-arg) falls back to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Including VIEW in a manage check means an admin holding only a `view` scope permission on the all-groups resource is considered able to manage groups. This method is used by `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup()` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`) and by `canManage(GroupModel)` callers, so a view-only admin could create, update, or delete top-level groups — a privilege escalation compared to canManage(GroupModel), which correctly checks only MANAGE. The expectedScopes for the global manage check should be MANAGE only.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

false_positives.candidate:
NPE when per-group resource and all-groups resource are both absent

In hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes), when `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns null, the code calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which returns null whenever the resource type resource does not exist or the schema is not supported for the resource server. The result is passed straight to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, causing a NullPointerException (500 error) instead of a clean `false` for admins without any group permissions. The analogous UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission has the same shape; at minimum the new GroupPermissionsV2 copy needs a null guard.

Removal of cached canViewGlobal causes repeated permission evaluation per subgroup

getSubGroups previously computed `canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()` once and short-circuited the filter. Now `auth.groups()::canView` is evaluated per subgroup. For an admin without the manage-users/view-users roles, each invocation of the V1 (and V2) global canView() runs a full authorization-policy evaluation against the admin permissions resource server, so listing a group with many subgroups performs N policy evaluations instead of one. The same pattern was removed in GroupsResource.getGroups. Cache the global result (or make canView() memoize) to avoid the per-element evaluation cost.

getScope NPEs when resourceType is null or unknown

In getScope, when the schema is supported, `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType)` is dereferenced without a null check. If a caller passes a null or unrecognized resourceType (e.g., a permission being created without a resource type before validation runs), this throws a NullPointerException instead of the intended ModelValidationException ("Scope %s was not found for resource type %s."). A null/unknown-type check with a meaningful validation error is needed.

requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method

The javadoc on requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says "Throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false" — copy-pasted from requireManageMembership. It should reference canManageMembers(GroupModel). Since this PR adds javadoc to the whole interface, the newly written contract text is wrong for this method and will mislead implementers/users of the evaluator.

resolveGroup only accepts the internal group id, unlike users/clients which also accept names

resolveUser and resolveClient fall back to lookup by username/clientId when the id lookup fails, but resolveGroup only does getGroupById. When creating a group policy via getOrCreateResource with a group name or path instead of the internal id, the method throws IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object..."). Either this asymmetry is intentional (then it deserves a comment) or the group path/name lookup is missing; as written, the API behaves inconsistently across resource types and callers passing a group path get a 500-level error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text

The fix for the HTML-sanitizer findings replaced the Lithuanian translation of totpStep1 with Italian text ('Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'). Lithuanian users of the account theme now see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. The same Italian string was also introduced in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties (line 71). Both should be restored to a proper Lithuanian translation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.

The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.
The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').
Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

false_positives.candidate:
Hardcoded per-key exceptions make the sanitizer brittle for future message content

normalizeValue() special-cases exactly the keys 'templateHelp', 'optimizeLookupHelp', 'linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*' and 'error-invalid-multivalued-size' to strip pseudo-HTML/MessageFormat fragments before sanitizing. Any new or existing message that legitimately contains a '<...>' fragment (such as docs examples or another choice-format key) will fail the build, and the only fix is to add another hardcoded key to this private method. A more general mechanism (e.g. an allowlist file or normalizing all {n,choice,...} patterns regardless of key) would avoid repeatedly patching the verifier.

Missing English sibling file crashes verification with a raw RuntimeException

verifySafeHtml() derives the English reference file by regex-replacing the locale suffix of the current file's absolute path, then opens it with new FileInputStream and wraps any IOException in a RuntimeException. If a locale properties file has no *_en.properties sibling in the same directory (e.g. a bundle that intentionally has no English file, or a file whose name does not match the assumed naming scheme), the RuntimeException escapes verify() (which only catches IOException) and aborts the whole build with an unhelpful stack trace instead of being reported as a per-file message or a MojoExecutionException. The failure mode should be a clean, actionable error.

error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from {{n}} to single-brace MessageFormat syntax in the JS UI resource

In the account console (React/i18next-based) message bundle, error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from '{{0}} ... {{2}} value(s).' to 'Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,...}'. All other keys in this file use double-brace interpolation (e.g. error-invalid-length on line 140), so the single-brace placeholders and the Java-MessageFormat choice pattern are not interpolated by this UI; users would see literal '{0}', '{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}' text. The same change was made to js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties (line 3138). If these keys are only rendered server-side via the Java base themes the change is fine, but then the JS copies should be verified against the UI's interpolation format before merging.

true_positives.golden_comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
rawTokenId null check checks grantType instead of rawTokenId

The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` twice; the second occurrence should check `rawTokenId`. As a result a null rawTokenId is silently accepted and the "rawTokenId" error message is never produced for an actual null rawTokenId, weakening the intended precondition.

true_positives.golden_comment: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Inverted comparison and wrong substring index in isAccessTokenId matcher

In isAccessTokenId the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted: it rejects the token when the shortcut MATCHES the expected grant, so tests will fail on correct token IDs and pass on wrong ones. Additionally the index is wrong: the grant-type shortcut occupies characters 4-5 of the 6-char prefix, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)` which grabs the last char of the token-type shortcut plus the first char of the grant shortcut. Every event assertion using this matcher (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) is broken.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

false_positives.candidate:
Decoding malformed/unrecognized token IDs throws instead of degrading gracefully

getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars, or when the session-type/token-type/grant shortcuts are unknown. This method is intended to be called on arbitrary incoming access tokens (e.g. tokens issued by another Keycloak version, a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider, or a custom grant with unregistered shortcut). A token with a colon but unexpected prefix format will cause an unhandled exception (500) in whatever endpoint later consumes this (introspection, userinfo, admin REST per the PR description). It should return UNKNOWN context rather than throwing, matching the no-colon fallback path.

Lazy cache refresh can silently corrupt bidirectional grant shortcut maps with duplicates

The duplicate-shortcut validation only runs once in postInit. getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut later mutate grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts for newly deployed providers without re-validating uniqueness: if a hot-deployed grant reuses an existing shortcut, grantsByShortcuts is overwritten so two grant types map to one shortcut while grantsToShortcuts keeps both, permanently desynchronizing encode/decode and producing tokens whose grant type decodes to the wrong grant.

Removal of public Context(Context) copy constructor is a source/behavioral break

The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was deleted and its behavior folded into the main constructor (which now reads grantType from formParams). Any external code subclassing or copying OAuth2GrantType.Context will no longer compile. Additionally, the grantType is now only captured at construction time from formParams; if setFormParams(...) is called afterwards (an existing public mutator), context.grantType becomes stale and will be encoded incorrectly into tokens issued via OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse.

Unused import TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory

The import org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory was added but the code uses the string constant OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE instead; the import is unused and should be removed.

getShortcut() added to SPI interface without default method breaks third-party implementations

OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a public SPI (server-spi-private) that third-party grant-type providers implement. Adding the abstract method `String getShortcut()` without a default implementation makes every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory fail to compile/load at runtime after upgrade. A `default String getShortcut() { return getId(); }` (or similar) would preserve compatibility.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

false_positives.candidate:
Federated recovery-code credential is never removed and codes are never consumed

When the recovery-codes credential lives in a user storage (federated), the code-consumption logic breaks in two ways. First, line 86 calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...) with the ID of the federated credential returned by getFederatedCredentialsStream(); that ID does not exist in Keycloak's local credential store, so the call is a silent no-op and the exhausted credential is never deleted from the user storage. Second, unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider (whose isValid() updates the credential to mark a code as used), there is no mechanism that consumes a code in the user storage after successful validation: the framework only calls the storage's isValid(), and nothing updates the stored credential. The net effect is that recovery codes created in user storage are single static secrets that remain valid indefinitely and can be replayed by an attacker who observed one, defeating the one-time property that recovery codes are supposed to have.

Raw (unhashed) recovery codes are sent to user storage via updateCredential

createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the plaintext generated codes to JSON and passes them as the challengeResponse of a UserCredentialModel to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Whatever a user-storage provider receives it may persist as-is (as the test provider in this PR does: it stores input.getChallengeResponse() directly as credentialData). This means the security of the codes (hashing vs. plaintext storage) is delegated entirely to third-party storage implementations, whereas the local provider always stores only hashes. Additionally, the fully-populated credentialModel with hashed codes that the caller built is discarded in this branch, so the provider loses the createdDate/userLabel metadata. At minimum this contract should be documented on the method so storage implementers know they are responsible for hashing, or the hashed model should be transferred.

Test does not verify that a used federated recovery code cannot be replayed

testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only performs a single successful login with one recovery code and never asserts that the same code is consumed (i.e., a second login with the same code should fail, and after 12 uses the credential should be exhausted and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action re-triggered). Since the production code has no path that consumes federated recovery codes (see the finding on RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator), the test as written passes while leaving the one-time-code property untested and broken. Add a replay/exhaustion assertion so this gap is caught.

getCredentials NPEs when the user is not present in the storage map

In the new getCredentials() override, getMyUser(user) can return null (users.get(...) of an unknown username), but the code dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check. Every other method that calls getMyUser (getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, isConfiguredFor) guards for null. A credential listing for a user that has been removed from the map will throw a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream, which can break unrelated credential queries.

true_positives.golden_comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
populateSubGroupCount can now propagate a null subGroupCount into GroupRepresentation

With GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount() changed to return null when the group has been concurrently deleted, GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount stores that null via representation.setSubGroupCount(null). Consumers that unbox getSubGroupCount() (the representation field is Long, and Admin UI / REST clients commonly treat it as a required count when populateSubGroupCount is requested) will see the field disappear from the JSON or risk NullPointerException on unboxing. Either the deleted-group case should be skipped (not emit/merge the representation) or the null contract should be documented and handled at this call site, rather than silently producing a representation with a missing subgroup count.

true_positives.golden_comment: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Concurrent-reader test does not join the reader thread, making it racy and ineffective

In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the background reader thread is started but never joined. The main thread sets deletedAll=true and immediately asserts that caughtExceptions is empty, so the test can pass while the reader thread is still mid-request or has not yet had a chance to hit the deleted-group window; any exception thrown after the assertion (or on the final iteration) is silently lost. The reader loop may also loop zero times if the deletes finish before the thread schedules, in which case the test exercises nothing. The test should join the thread (e.g., set a done flag, interrupt/join, then assert) to reliably reproduce the race it is meant to cover.

false_positives.candidate:
LazyModel supplier caches a previously-resolved delegate, so a later concurrent delete still returns a stale model

getSubGroupsCount now guards against modelSupplier.get() returning null, but modelSupplier is a LazyModel that caches the delegate once resolved. If the underlying group was already resolved through this adapter (e.g., via getSubGroupsStream(search, ...) at lines 254-268, which use the same supplier) and is then deleted by another thread, modelSupplier.get() returns the cached non-null GroupModel and getSubGroupsCount() is invoked on a deleted group, which can still fail. The null guard only covers the case where the model was never resolved before the delete; the fix is incomplete for repeated access through the same cached adapter.

Inverted comparison and wrong substring index in isAccessTokenId matcher

In isAccessTokenId the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted: it rejects the token when the shortcut MATCHES the expected grant, so tests will fail on correct token IDs and pass on wrong ones. Additionally the index is wrong: the grant-type shortcut occupies characters 4-5 of the 6-char prefix, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)` which grabs the last char of the token-type shortcut plus the first char of the grant shortcut. false_positives.candidate:

getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars, or when the session-type/token-type/grant shortcuts are unknown. This method is intended to be called on arbitrary incoming access tokens (e.g. tokens issued by another Keycloak version, a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider, or a custom grant with unregistered shortcut). A token with a colon but unexpected prefix format will cause an unhandled exception (500) in whatever endpoint later consumes this (introspection, userinfo, admin REST per the PR description). It should return UNKNOWN context rather than throwing, matching the no-colon fallback path.

getShortcut() added to SPI interface without default method breaks third-party implementations

OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a public SPI (server-spi-private) that third-party grant-type providers implement. Adding the abstract method `String getShortcut()` without a default implementation makes every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory fail to compile/load at runtime after upgrade. A `default String getShortcut() { return getId(); }` (or similar) would preserve compatibility.

Removal of public Context(Context) copy constructor is a source/behavioral break

The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was deleted and its behavior folded into the main constructor (which now reads grantType from formParams). Any external code subclassing or copying OAuth2GrantType.Context will no longer compile. Additionally, the grantType is now only captured at construction time from formParams; if setFormParams(...) is called afterwards (an existing public mutator), context.grantType becomes stale and will be encoded incorrectly into tokens issued via OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse.

Lazy cache refresh can silently corrupt bidirectional grant shortcut maps with duplicates

false_positives.candidate:
Federated recovery-code credential is never removed and codes are never consumed

When the recovery-codes credential lives in a user storage (federated), the code-consumption logic breaks in two ways. First, line 86 calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...) with the ID of the federated credential returned by getFederatedCredentialsStream(); that ID does not exist in Keycloak's local credential store, so the call is a silent no-op and the exhausted credential is never deleted from the user storage. Second, unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider (whose isValid() updates the credential to mark a code as used), there is no mechanism that consumes a code in the user storage after successful validation: the framework only calls the storage's isValid(), and nothing updates the stored credential. The net effect is that recovery codes created in user storage are single static secrets that remain valid indefinitely and can be replayed by an attacker who observed one, defeating the one-time property that recovery codes are supposed to have.

Raw (unhashed) recovery codes are sent to user storage via updateCredential

createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes the plaintext generated codes to JSON and passes them as the challengeResponse of a UserCredentialModel to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). Whatever a user-storage provider receives it may persist as-is (as the test provider in this PR does: it stores input.getChallengeResponse() directly as credentialData). This means the security of the codes (hashing vs. plaintext storage) is delegated entirely to third-party storage implementations, whereas the local provider always stores only hashes. Additionally, the fully-populated credentialModel with hashed codes that the caller built is discarded in this branch, so the provider loses the createdDate/userLabel metadata. At minimum this contract should be documented on the method so storage implementers know they are responsible for hashing, or the hashed model should be transferred.

getCredentials NPEs when the user is not present in the storage map

In the new getCredentials() override, getMyUser(user) can return null (users.get(...) of an unknown username), but the code dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check. Every other method that calls getMyUser (getDisableableCredentialTypesStream, isConfiguredFor) guards for null. A credential listing for a user that has been removed from the map will throw a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream, which can break unrelated credential queries.

Test does not verify that a used federated recovery code cannot be replayed

testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only performs a single successful login with one recovery code and never asserts that the same code is consumed (i.e., a second login with the same code should fail, and after 12 uses the credential should be exhausted and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action re-triggered). Since the production code has no path that consumes federated recovery codes (see the finding on RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator), the test as written passes while leaving the one-time-code property untested and broken. Add a replay/exhaustion assertion so this gap is caught.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

getClientsWithPermission iterates resources found by type Clients and adds resource.getName() for each granted resource. The "Clients" all-resource itself has type Clients, so if the admin holds a scope permission on it (granted for all clients), the literal string "Clients" is added to the returned set — a value that is not a client ID. Worse, the intended semantics of an all-clients grant (the caller should see every client) are not handled at all: callers filtering client lists by this set will get an empty/incorrect result even though the admin is allowed to act on all clients.
